one_month_reasoning: No scheduled earnings inside the window: Q3 2026 results have not been dated, and DigitalOcean reported Q3 2025 in early November and Q2 2026 on Aug 4, so Q3 most likely lands in the first week of November, just after 2026-11-01. The Q3 guide ($304-307M, +32-34% y/y, above the $294M consensus) makes a beat likely, but that event most likely falls outside the window. The risks inside the window are an unscheduled preliminary release or capital-markets action (in July they pre-announced, then sold stock); the 2026 converts mature Dec 1; and AI-infrastructure sentiment swings. The stock rallied from about $106 (Form 144 sale price, Sep 3) to about $140 by Sep 21, so momentum and reversal roughly cancel. With no scheduled catalyst, I use an almost symmetric lognormal centred on $140 with sigma = 82%/3.5 ≈ 23% for the month and a tiny negative drift.

fair_value.method: Blend of 40% P/E (45x CY2028E EPS $2.48 = $112), 40% EV/EBITDA (22x CY2028E GAAP-basis EBITDA $757M less ~$1.0B net debt incl. finance leases, on 125M shares = $125), and 20% DCF (11% WACC, 4% terminal growth = $80). That gives about $111 for October 2027, versus $140 today.

inputs_detail.derivation: $1.84 x 1.35. Assumes 2028 revenue growth of about 35% after >50% in 2027 (mgmt outlook, sources 1 and 7), with the 155MW pipeline 80% online by end-2027 and RPO of $894M over a 3.7-yr life (source 2). EPS grows in line with revenue because GPU depreciation (D&A was up 65% y/y in Q2) holds back operating leverage.

Peer CY2027 P/E median is 23.8x (range 14.5-221x, n=7 profitable peers). I apply the same growth-adjusted multiple as peers: median PEG ≈1.3 (23.8x / ~18% EPS growth) times DOCN's ~35% 2028E EPS growth gives ~45x. That sits inside the range, between FSLY (41x) and NET (221x).

inputs_detail.derivation: $1.81B x 1.35. 2027 capacity comes online (60MW mainly in 2027, plus 20MW in late 2027/early 2028), and RPO of $894M recognises $366M within 12 months.
TTM EBITDA $308.6M / TTM revenue $1.01B = 30.6%, held flat. This is the same basis I use for peers (TTM GAAP EBITDA margin x CY revenue), not the company's 40% adjusted EBITDA, which excludes SBC.

Peer CY2027 median is 15.6x (range 7.3-67.1x, n=8). DOCN gets a premium of about 40%, still below NBIS's 29x, for revenue growth of 35-54% against a median of roughly 19% for profitable peers. That growth is visible in contracted RPO, which is 12x y/y.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue 2028-32: 2.43/3.04/3.65/4.20/4.70B; unlevered FCF after all capex (incl. leased equipment) 6%->20% of revenue; WACC 11%; terminal growth 4%; EV $11.0B less $1.0B net debt / 125M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Starts from consensus $1.81B for 2027 and decays toward mature cloud growth.

FY26 adjusted FCF margin guide is 11-13%, and Q1 2026 was 1% during the build. Adjusted FCF excludes equipment financed through leases ($415M of finance-lease ROU assets added in 1H26), so a true all-in FCF margin starts lower.
High-beta (82% realized vol) equity-funded business with little net debt.

bear.story: AI GPU capacity loosens or one of the nine-figure inference customers churns or downsizes. 2027 growth comes in near 35-40% rather than >50%, gross margin keeps compressing (55% in Q2 vs 60% a year earlier) as GPU depreciation and lease interest build, and more equity or lease funding is needed. The multiple falls toward the peer median of about 30x on roughly $2.1 of CY2028E EPS.

base.story: 2027 growth beats 50% (about $1.8B), the 155MW of capacity comes online on schedule, and CY2028E EPS is about $2.5. The market keeps paying about 55x forward, so the stock is roughly flat as delivery offsets multiple compression.

bull.story: More nine-figure commitments and a 2027 guide implying 60%+ growth; RPO goes above $2B. CY2028E EPS reaches about $3.0 and the market pays about 75x as DOCN is re-rated with AI inference platforms.

comps_summary.peer_range: Basis is calendar 2027 for every peer (ORCL, MSFT and IREN calendarised). P/E is 14.5x (ORCL) to 221x (NET), n=7, with the neoclouds not meaningful because of losses. EV/EBITDA, computed as TTM GAAP EBITDA margin x CY2027 consensus revenue, is 7.3x (CRWV) to 67.1x (IREN), n=8, with NET and FSLY not meaningful because GAAP EBITDA is negative.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: Today DOCN trades at 76x CY2027 EPS ($140.07/$1.84) and about 32x CY2027 EBITDA on the same basis, both far above the medians. My multiples are 45x P/E (about 1.9x the median, inside the range) and 22x EV/EBITDA (about 1.4x the median, inside the range).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium rests only on structurally higher revenue growth that is visible in contracts: RPO is $894M, up 12x y/y, with a 3.7-year weighted life and $366M due within 12 months. Committed capacity is 155MW, and management has kept a >50% 2027 growth outlook since May and reaffirmed it in August. I size the premium on growth (equal PEG to peers), not on narrative. I do not go further for three reasons: EPS growth (+26% consensus 2027) is far below revenue growth because of GPU depreciation; gross margin is falling; and returns on the new capacity are unproven. That is why I stay well below where the stock trades.

thesis_break_reason: At $80 the stock trades at about 43x CY2027 consensus EPS and roughly 18x EBITDA, close to the peer medians. Getting there would most likely mean the >50% 2027 growth outlook or the nine-figure AI commitments behind the $894M RPO had broken (customer churn, capacity delays, or GPU pricing collapse), not ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Primary filings show genuine acceleration. Revenue grew 29% in Q2 (22% in Q1), the Q3 guide is +32-34%, RPO is $894M (12x) with multiple nine-figure annual commitments, and management has said since May that it expects >50% growth in 2027 (consensus is $1.81B). The footnotes temper this. Gross margin fell from 59.9% to 55.0%; GAAP operating income fell y/y; adjusted FCF in Q1 was 1% of revenue; $415M of GPU equipment came in through finance leases; a new MUFG lease facility of up to $1.025B is planned; and shares outstanding rose from 92M to 117.6M in 2026 (two equity raises, one swapping $472M of converts for 12.5M shares). At $140 the stock trades at 76x CY2027 consensus EPS and about 32x CY2027 EBITDA, against calendar-2027 peer medians of 23.8x and 15.6x across ten cloud and AI-infrastructure peers. Growth-adjusted multiples plus a DCF give a fair value of about $111, below the sell-side average target of $175. Momentum and the AI narrative are strong, though, so the base case is roughly flat ($135) and I set the distribution median at about $128 rather than at fair value. I use a lognormal sigma of 0.68 (below the 82% realized vol, since part of that came from a re-rating that is unlikely to repeat at the same speed), which gives P(≥$140) ≈ 0.45 and fat tails both ways (P(≥$245) ≈ 0.17, P(<$70) ≈ 0.19). The scenario mean is about $138. Research limits: Yahoo would not load analysis pages for NET, EQIX, DLR or DOCN; EQIX and DLR were dropped (REIT P/E is not meaningful anyway); NET's 2027 EPS comes from StockAlarm; peer forward EBITDA is my own constant-margin estimate. No option data was used.
